elements.element: Customer (Sparkling) may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "The consent requirement ... does not apply to an assignment by Sparkling to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: paragraph (d) retained ("Neither party may assign ... without the written consent of the other party") plus "Sparkling's consent to an assignment by Garman shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "Garman may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Sparkling"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "a change of control of Sparkling does not give Garman any right to terminate this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Vendor-side successor assignment still requires consent; only "Sparkling's consent ... shall not be unreasonably withheld"
no notice mechanic appears in the inserted sentence

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Sparkling's consent to an assignment by Garman shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All five atomic preferred elements are satisfied by a single inserted sentence: Customer affiliate assignment, Customer successor assignment (merger, acquisition, sale of substantially all assets), reasonableness standard on Customer's consent to Vendor assignment, absolute bar on assignment to a Customer competitor, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.

Minimality holds: paragraph (d) is untouched and the only other edit is a four-word conforming cross-reference in 3(c) ("or as permitted by this Agreement") needed so the earlier sublicence/assignment bar does not re-impose the consent requirement on Customer.
No fallback-only mechanic (mutual successor assignment on written notice) was imported into the operative text; it is mentioned only in the non-operative comment, which is correct.
Intent preserved: no undefined terms, no contradiction with (d), and the transfer/lease/export/sublicence restrictions in (c) remain effective except as permitted elsewhere in the Agreement.
Fallback is independently incomplete (no mutual successor right, no notice), but the locked target level is preferred and it is fully met.
